trajectory_summary: This call is procedurally efficient but emotionally flat: the rep never asks why the customer is interested in solar, never anchors the $300/month bill as a reason to act, and books the appointment purely on scheduling logistics. The three-way call with Dominion Energy consumed roughly seven of the eleven minutes and was handled competently, but it substituted for real qualification rather than supplementing it.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (noon) are agreed, and the rep frames it as the specialist dropping by, indicating an in-person appointment; no co-owner or spouse was mentioned anywhere in the call.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: The the bills average around that about 300 a month.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep acknowledges the figure with a bare 'Okay. Gotcha.' and moves directly to kWh usage questions; the flip should have landed here or when booking the appointment, tying the $300/month pain to the reason to see the design.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks what interested the customer in solar; the customer's own line ('I don't know if I want it or not. I just wanna find out what it cost') is the closest thing to a stated reason, and it's a disqualifying-sounding one that the rep never probed or reframed.

script_coverage.quote: I'm with Ion. We're just calling you because we had a we had a request here that you were looking at solar for the home.
Was that for the 1027 In Long Road in in Ridgeland, South Carolina?
Do you know your login on on the Dominion website by chance?
The the bills average around that about 300 a month.
we could add them to the phone line here, and we could have them read it off to you

primary_coaching_focus.topic: incomplete button-up / no interest anchor at close
primary_coaching_focus.quote: is this a good day to show you that design and kinda go over the price with you?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment was booked purely on scheduling convenience — no bill flip, no interest reason, and no button-up handshake (hour block, no-driving instruction, 'is that fair?', text-follow-up promise). This is the highest-leverage, most fixable gap: the appointment is booked but structurally thin, raising no-show risk on a call that otherwise ran efficient logistics.

key_moments.quote: I don't know if I want it or not. I just wanna find out what it cost.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the customer handing the rep a direct opening to ask 'what got you looking into solar in the first place?' The rep instead validates the price-only frame and moves straight to logistics.

key_moments.quote: The the bills average around that about 300 a month.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer gives a concrete, sizable bill figure unprompted-ish, but the rep only acknowledges it ('Okay. Gotcha.') and moves immediately into kWh usage questions without any emotional reflection.

key_moments.quote: Do you know your login on on the Dominion website by chance?
key_moments.stewart_read: Good process instinct — rep quickly identifies the customer doesn't have easy bill access and moves to find an alternative path rather than stalling.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. If you just wanna hang out for a second, I'll add them to the phone so it'll be a three way call.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep commits seven minutes of call time to a utility IVR and live rep read-back. It resolves the bill-data gap completely and accurately (12 months of kWh), which is a strong data outcome for the design phase.
